topic.title: Introduction
topic.description: Overview of math, characters, and strings

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s explore the building blocks of Java programming! Today, we’ll cover:

• How computers handle numbers and math
• The difference between characters and strings
• Why these concepts matter in real code

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you’re building a digital recipe app. Math helps calculate ingredient quantities, while characters and strings let users type their favorite recipes.

**Numbers in Java**
• Java has different number types (like `int` for whole numbers, `double` for decimals)
• Example: `int eggs = 12;` stores how many eggs you have

**Characters vs Strings**
• A *character* is a single letter/symbol (`'A'`, `'$'`, `'7'`) 
• A *string* is a sequence of characters (`"Hello!"`, `"12 eggs"`)

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: The Math class provides methods for common mathematical operations
The char type stores a single Unicode character enclosed in single quotes
The String class represents sequences of characters and is immutable
printf allows formatted output using format specifiers like %d, %f, and %s
This chapter builds on variables and expressions from elementary programming

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Numbers (`int`, `double`) power calculations in apps. `char` = single character, `String` = text. Practice mixing math and strings for dynamic output. Ready to learn loops next – they’ll make this 10x more powerful.

questions.question: Which Java class provides mathematical methods like sqrt, pow, and abs?
questions.explanation: The Math class in Java provides commonly used mathematical methods like Math.sqrt(), Math.pow(), Math.abs(), Math.max(), and Math.min().

questions.question: Which of the following data types represents a single character in Java?
questions.explanation: The char data type represents a single character in Java. It uses single quotes (e.g., 'A'). String represents a sequence of characters and uses double quotes.
